children: has extended a historically long bear market after dropping to a new cycle low over the weekend, even as the depth of the decline remains comparatively modest and several indicators signal oversold conditions, Grayscale stated.

On Saturday, November 21, the cryptocurrency fell to $55K, moving below the prior low of $58K set on June 30. The move stretches the current bear market to at least 411 days—the longest on record—while the peak-to-trough drawdown of 56% ranks as the shallowest.

The latest decline also wiped out the entirety of gains linked to a recent NVIDIA-related rally in less than six hours, highlighting marked relative weakness. Bitcoin has returned to levels last seen during the summer, near $60K as equity markets remain in a broader downtrend despite Monday’s pop.

Price action and fund-flow data both point to oversold conditions. Global crypto exchange-traded products recorded more than $2 billion in outflows last week, while stablecoin redemptions have accelerated. Futures open interest for bitcoin
has retreated to summer lows. In options markets, the implied volatility curve is deeply inverted, with investors paying elevated premiums for downside protection.

Grayscale said bitcoin and other leading digital assets appear oversold, but indicated that the near-term outlook will depend more on risks tied to artificial intelligence than on underlying blockchain fundamentals.

title: Grayscale: Bitcoin is oversold, but AI risks now drive the outlook
